mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6.5% within a single month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 6.5% in one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6.5% in a single month (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates supply-side weakness, which raises input costs and reduces profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO is below its 12-month MA for four months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their prior 12-month averages signals a dual tightening of monetary policy and accelerating inflation, which erodes real purchasing power and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month averages (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated increase in both personal income (implied by PAYEMS growth) and housing starts (HOUST) above their 6-month moving averages signals a robust recovery in household demand, which boosts corporate revenue expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and HOUST both exceed 6-month moving averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and HOUST exceed their 6-month moving averages (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals improving labor market conditions, which increases consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month MA for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS is above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal savings (implied by RSAFS growth) combined with a flat or declining consumption series (GDPC1) signals a shift from spending to saving, which typically precedes a future consumption rebound and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS rises while GDPC1 is flat or declining for three consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when RSAFS rises and GDPC1 is flat/declining for three quarters (t-test p > 0.05).
